summary: Integration brief: ARDA Agent Loop proposes autonomous work, while tool-gate independently evaluates each proposed tool invocation and emits allow, deny, or review_required receipts without executing it (README.md:5-13, README.md:51-56). Their shared safety boundary is the transition from agent intent to runtime side effects: proposals must become explicit invocation envelopes and pass deterministic target, trace, idempotency, risk, and review checks before execution (README.md:17-20, README.md:146-158). Actionable integration: place tool-gate directly between Agent Loop and the execution runtime; execute only allow receipts, route review_required receipts to Council/HUD for operator approval, and audit denials and receipts. Agent Loop risk: a runtime path that accepts its proposals directly could bypass policy review. tool-gate risk: metadata is caller-supplied and the gate provides neither authentication nor sandboxing, so untrusted or incorrectly classified metadata could understate mutation or risk unless a trusted catalog and enforcement layer validate it (README.md:5-13, README.md:156-158; src/types.rs:21-30). The declared clean-tree check passed before inspection and again afterward; no files were modified.
